notes.b1/j1/F-r1: Bold dark tin-themed design with a tidy bento popover, but the popover overlaps hero text and the closed state shows no bento at all.
notes.b1/j1/Q-r1: Bento panel with quantity stepper works but opens narrow, covers page copy awkwardly, and the 'Nothing selected yet' state is clunky.
notes.b1/j1/A-r1: Rich bento menu with roast chips, sliders, toggles and accordions, though the tiny type is dense and the toast overlaps the headline.
notes.b1/j1/Q-r2: Functional small bento with roast, grind and quantity controls, but plain, sparse and the bento sits in an unstyled page.
notes.b1/j1/A-r2: Clean dark-pill nav opening a well-composed bento with subscription and guides, a bit generic and small in text.
notes.b1/j1/F-r2: Strongest bento: colorful tiles collapse to an icon strip and expand into a rich illustrated grid, with state readout and keyboard hints.
notes.b1/j2/Q-r2: Working collapsible pill with a small bento of controls, but the open panel is cramped and the page is nearly empty.
notes.b1/j2/A-r2: Polished nav with a real bento panel of interactive cards (roast, subscription, accordion guides), though the open panel pushes content down.
notes.b1/j2/F-r2: Folded state is a tidy row of tiles that expands into a bento with page-change feedback, but the folded state is plain and the status chips are clutter.
notes.b1/j2/A-r1: Richest and most bento-like: varied tile sizes with illustrations, clear fold and unfold, tiles that change the page, and good keyboard cues.
notes.b1/j2/Q-r1: Good bento content and working cart stepper, but the open panel is narrow and awkwardly overlaps the hero text.
notes.b1/j2/F-r1: Distinctive dark tin theme with a floating bento popover; the popover covers the hero and the tiles are fairly small.
notes.b1/j3/A-r2: Clean pill nav opening a bento grid of beans, subscription, guides, cafes, saved; polished but sparse and fairly conventional.
notes.b1/j3/F-r2: Illustrated, colourful bento tiles that fold to a strip and reflow into a rich grid with working tile selection, though the folded state is not fully hidden and mobile loses labels.
notes.b1/j3/Q-r2: Compact bento panel with roast chips, grind toggle and quantity stepper that reflects in the button, but visually plain and small.
notes.b1/j3/F-r1: Bold dark tin-themed design with a popover bento grid that overlaps the hero and sits somewhat cramped, but is distinctive and works.
notes.b1/j3/A-r1: Colourful bento panel with working roast slider, subscription picker, accordions and toggles that update live page state, and a cohesive warm look.
notes.b1/j3/Q-r1: Menu panel opens narrow and left-aligned, overlapping and clipping the hero text, which looks unfinished despite a working cart stepper.
notes.b2/j1/F-r3: Playful stack-to-grid idea with a tilted bento tile layout, but the nav is oddly offset on desktop and the tiles are thin on real function.
notes.b2/j1/Q-r3: Cohesive Ember & Oak bento with working roast, subscription, bag and collapsible tiles plus a status line and Escape and outside-click close.
notes.b2/j1/A-r3: Polished, genuine menu-ordering bento with varied tile sizes, though the size chips on the featured card have weak contrast.
notes.b2/j1/Q-r4: Compact dark floating nav bar that unfolds into a tight bento with a bag stepper, newsletter signup and Escape hint; tidy and legible.
notes.b2/j1/A-r4: Feature-rich bento (roast, bag, plan, cafes, guides) with a state readout, but the big dark card has dead space and the brand name drops out on mobile.
notes.b2/j1/F-r4: Bold editorial look with an unfolding bento panel, but the panel overlaps and cuts the hero headline and the layout feels cramped.
notes.b2/j2/Q-r4: Tidy dark pill nav that opens a compact six-tile bento with a bag stepper and roast picker, but sparse content and small tiles.
notes.b2/j2/A-r4: Rich bento with working roast, subscription and cafe controls and a visible state readout, though dense and a little debug-looking.
notes.b2/j2/F-r4: Bold Kiln and Kettle branding and a floating bento panel with working controls, but the panel covers the hero text and is fairly small on a cramped layout.
notes.b2/j2/A-r3: Clean full-width bento with featured blend, categories, order list, milk options and a running total; cohesive and usable, with a blank page at rest.
notes.b2/j2/Q-r3: Most complete and polished bento: expanding tiles, roast and subscription toggles, bag, cafe select, with Escape and outside-click close and a cohesive palette.
notes.b2/j2/F-r3: Stacked-tins concept with playful tilted tiles and a distinctive look, but the tiles are small and mobile puts the menu below the hero.
notes.b2/j3/A-r4: Rich, well-built bento with working roast, subscription, cafe and guide controls, but the logo text vanishes on mobile and the debug state line clutters the page.
notes.b2/j3/F-r4: Bold poster-style page with a tidy floating bento panel and working controls, though the panel covers the headline and the intro text is cramped.
notes.b2/j3/Q-r4: Compact, coherent bento drop-down with varied tiles and a working bag stepper, but fairly thin in content.
notes.b2/j3/F-r3: Inventive stacked-tins concept with a good grid, but the tiles are small, rotated and text-light, and the header sits awkwardly.
notes.b2/j3/A-r3: Ambitious ordering UI with a good tile layout, but the size pills are nearly invisible on the dark card and the page is empty at rest.
notes.b2/j3/Q-r3: Cleanest and most complete bento menu, with collapsible tiles, roast and bag state, Escape and click-outside handling, and a layout that holds up on mobile.
